title: The Mischievous Dog
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: There was once a Dog who used to snap at people and bite them without any provocation, and who was a great nuisance to every one who came to his master's house. So his master fastened a bell round his neck to warn people of his presence. The Dog was very proud of the bell, and strutted about tinkling it with immense satisfaction. But an old dog came up to him and said, "The fewer airs you give yourself the better, my friend. You don't think, do you, that your bell was given you as a reward of merit? On the contrary, it is a badge of disgrace."
Notoriety is often mistaken for fame.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Dog use to do to people?
options: Follow them quietly wherever they went
Bark loudly but never come close
Snap at them and bite them without any provocation
Hide from them whenever they arrived

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does the Dog's master fasten a bell round his neck?
options: To warn people of the Dog's presence
To help him find the Dog if it wanders off
To reward the Dog for guarding the house
To keep other dogs away from him

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Dog feel about wearing the bell?
options: Embarrassed by it
Frightened of its sound
Annoyed by its weight
Very proud of it

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Dog behave once he has the bell?
options: He tries to remove it with his paws
He struts about tinkling it with immense satisfaction
He hides indoors to avoid the noise
He barks constantly to drown out the sound

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who corrects the Dog's understanding of the bell?
options: His master
A passing stranger
An old dog
Another young dog

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the old dog say the bell really is?
options: A badge of disgrace
A reward of merit
A sign of good breeding
A gift from his master's friends

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Dog mistakenly believe the bell is something to be proud of?
options: He was told directly by his master that it was an honor
He has seen other dogs praised for wearing similar bells
He does not know that the bell makes any sound at all
He assumes any attention drawn to him must mean he has done something admirable

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what is the old dog trying to teach the Dog with his remark?
options: That bells should never be worn by any dog
That being noticed is not the same as being respected
That his master no longer wants him in the house
That biting people is sometimes an acceptable habit

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Dog was a "nuisance" to visitors?
options: A source of amusement and delight
A source of comfort and safety
A source of annoyance or trouble
A source of pride for the household

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: Being talked about is not the same as being admired
A bell is always a sign of a dog's good behavior
Old dogs are wiser than young dogs in every case
Masters should never punish a mischievous dog

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what problem does the Dog cause at his master's house?
options: He refuses to eat the food he is given
He frightens away the other dogs in the yard
He digs holes throughout the garden
He is a great nuisance to everyone who visits

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the old dog call the Dog as he speaks to him?
options: "Young master"
"My friend"
"Poor fellow"
"Little brother"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what question does the old dog ask about the bell?
options: Whether the Dog knows how much the bell cost
Whether the Dog wants to trade it for food
Whether the Dog thinks it was given as a reward of merit
Whether the Dog can hear it ringing at all

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the master choose a bell rather than some other way to control the Dog?
options: Its sound gives people a warning before the Dog can reach them
It is the cheapest way to identify the Dog if it wanders off
It matches the color of the Dog's collar
It was recommended to him by the old dog

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Dog's strutting suggest about how he sees himself after getting the bell?
options: He is trying to hide the fact that he is ashamed
He is imitating another dog he admires
He no longer wants to bite visitors at all
He believes the attention it brings makes him important

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean to "give yourself airs"?
options: To breathe more heavily than usual
To act as though you are more important than you are
To speak too softly to be heard
To avoid the company of other dogs

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A dog loses his bell after a fight with an older dog
A dog is praised by his master for wearing a new bell
A dog mistakes a mark of shame for a badge of honor, until an older dog corrects him
A dog stops biting visitors after hearing the old dog's words
